name: chip-graphics
title: Chip graphics
description: Chip stacks for an amount in the application's denominations, and bets moving to the pot, for web, Apple and Android.

facilities.description: Chip piles, denomination breakdown, bets and winnings in motion

text.purpose: `chip-graphics` turns an amount into stacks of discs and moves them. A greedy breakdown picks the largest denominations first and starts another stack after twelve chips; discs are drawn with a dashed edge and the value of the top chip; the amount is written under the pile. It also plans motion: every bet moving from in front of its owner to the pot at once, winnings moving from the pot to each winner, a bet moving from a seat to its spot (an all in being slower and larger), with the position of a pile at any moment of a flight. The denominations and their colours are settings, so a game of tokens worth 100, 20, 5 and 1 uses the same code as a casino set. It draws no cards and knows no game rules.
text.userInputs: `denominations`: the chip values, written as an optional name then whole numbers separated by spaces, always including 1 so every amount can be made: `casino 5000 1000 500 100 25 5 1` (default) or `tokens 100 20 5 1`. An aepm string setting may hold only letters, digits, spaces and hyphens, so the list cannot use commas; code may also pass an array. `chipColours`: the name of a colour set then optional `denomination-rrggbb` entries: `casino` (default) uses the casino colours, `mine 1000-e07b2a 25-2e8b57` overrides two; a denomination without an entry keeps its casino colour, or gets a spare colour if the casino set has none for it; ink is chosen to read on the disc. The amount label's border is the theme's primary colour.
text.integration: Web: link `web/chips.css`; call `pileEl(amount, { settings: { denominations, chipColours }, size, label, format })`; plan motion with `sweepToPot`, `awardPot` and `betFlight` using spots from the `table-layout` component, and play it with `launchFlights(container, flights, { project })`, where `project` turns a spot (a fraction of the table) into pixels. Apple: compile `ChipModel.swift` anywhere and `ChipViews.swift` in UIKit targets with the theme's Swift files; `ChipStyle(denominations:chipColours:)` once near the root with `.chipStyle(...)`; use `ChipPile` and `ChipFlightLayer`. Android: add `ChipModel.kt` and `ChipViews.kt` to a Compose module with the theme's Kotlin files and provide `LocalChipStyle`. Seat positions, the pot spot, the decision of when to sweep and what the amounts mean are the application's.
text.infrastructure: None. Local drawing only; no accounts, network or deployment.
text.verification: Node tests check the breakdown (largest first, adding back to the amount for many amounts, twelve to a stack, other denomination sets and a missing 1 refused), the settings grammar, colours (casino, overrides, spare colours, readable ink), pile layout (stack spacing, lift, which chips carry a value), short value text, the DOM of `pileEl`, and flights (sweep, award, the rise of a bet, an all in being slower, easing, landing order) including launching real timed flights against a stand-in page and cancelling them, and that the OpenRPC interface's setting patterns accept and refuse what the parsers do, its limits and flight shape match the code, and every method it lists is an exported web function. The Apple check compiles and runs `tests/apple/main.swift` for macOS, comparing 36 breakdowns over three denomination sets, pile layouts, colours and flights with the TypeScript output, then type-checks all Swift with the theme's against the iOS simulator SDK. The Android check compares the same breakdowns and layouts (`tests/android/Expected.kt`); kotlinc was not available where this was written, so it has not been run, and `ChipViews.kt` (Compose) is only compiled by the application's Gradle build. Pixels are not compared.
text.scenarios: A hand of 1,337 chips shows as one orange 1k chip, three black 100s, a green 25, two red 5s and two grey 1s; a call sends the caller's chips from their seat to the bet spot; at the end of a betting round every bet sweeps into the pot together; a winner's share flies from the pot to their stack; a game of tokens worth 100, 20, 5 and 1 shows blue 100 chips; a raise to everything is slower, larger and glows.
text.updates: Patch updates replace files only. The component keeps no data; removal deletes its files and the application's imports of them.

agentInstructions: Select `ourapps-ae/chip-graphics`; connect `theme` to the theme component. Set `denominations` from the recipe's chips answer (starting chips and blinds decide which denominations are useful; always include 1) and leave `chipColours` at `casino` unless the user wants other colours.
developerInstructions: Choose denominations so a typical stack is a handful of chips (a stack over twelve becomes two). Pass spots from `table-layout` as fractions of the table to the flight functions. Keep `chip-model` the single source of truth; regenerate the Swift and Kotlin fixtures with `node tests/make-fixtures.ts` after any change.

suitability.notes: Pure library; no provider limits apply.
